description: Exact hand-built circuit, no LayerNorm: attention gathers the 5 digits, MLP finds slope m by testing dy == m*dx (m=1..5), computes y1+m*(xq-x1) with ReLU gating, one-hot of the answer, then tens digit at pos 11 and units digit at pos 12 via a position flag.
Ablation of V1: position-flag gating removed from layer 4, so tens and units logits are both active at every position. Expected to fail.
V1 with attention sharpness BETA=8 (match score 2 instead of 40): tests how sharp the copy heads must be.
V1 with attention sharpness BETA=16 (match score 4 instead of 40): sharpness sweep point.
V1 with attention sharpness BETA=24 (match score 6 instead of 40): sharpness sweep point.
V1 with attention sharpness BETA=40 (match score 10 instead of 40): sharpness sweep point.
V1 with attention sharpness BETA=80 (match score 20 instead of 40): sharpness sweep point.
V1 (BETA=40) with head logit scale 1 instead of 10: checks that the output margin is not critical.
V1 (BETA=40, logit scale 10) with MLP hidden width d_ff=165, the minimum the circuit's largest layer (one-hot of the answer) needs.
V1 (BETA=40, logit scale 10) with MLP hidden width d_ff=128, below the 165 the one-hot layer needs: expected to crash on indexing.
V1 (BETA=40, logit scale 10) with a narrower residual stream: d_model=112, 7 heads (one per gathered prompt position), d_ff=165. All 112 registers are used exactly.
V1 (d_model=112 version) with standard nn.LayerNorm restored in every block: normalization destroys the exact digit/indicator scale, so accuracy is expected to drop.
Depth-3 rewrite (3 blocks, d_ff=825): the answer one-hot is computed directly from the slope indicators in block 2 (gated by I_m with big-M 200), removing the separate A step.
Depth-3 variant with big-M gating constant 50 (too small: the ungated candidates can leak into the one-hot). Expected to fail.
Depth-3 variant with big-M gating constant 100: the smallest value that keeps every ungated candidate's ReLU at zero (A_m - v + 1 <= 100).
Depth-3 variant with big-M gating constant 20 (far too small): ungated slope candidates leak into the one-hot. Expected to fail badly.
Depth-3 variant with big-M gating constant 75: between the 50 (99%) and 100 (100%) points of the gate-constant sweep.
Depth-3 variant (gate 100) with attention sharpness BETA=8: attention sweep in the 3-block model.
Depth-3 variant (gate 100) with attention sharpness BETA=16: attention sweep in the 3-block model.
Depth-3 variant (gate 100) with attention sharpness BETA=24: attention sweep in the 3-block model.
Depth-3 variant (gate 100) with attention sharpness BETA=32: attention sweep in the 3-block model.
Depth-3 variant (gate 100) with attention sharpness BETA=12: attention sweep in the 3-block model.
Depth-3 variant (gate 100) with attention sharpness BETA=20: attention sweep in the 3-block model.
Depth-3 variant (gate 100) with attention sharpness BETA=28: attention sweep in the 3-block model.
Depth-3 variant (gate 100) with attention sharpness BETA=60: attention sweep in the 3-block model.
Depth-3 variant (gate 100) with attention sharpness BETA=4 (near-uniform attention): attention sweep in the 3-block model.
Depth-3 variant (gate 100) with attention sharpness BETA=2 (almost uniform attention): lower end of the attention sweep.
Depth-3 variant (gate 100) with attention sharpness BETA=1000 (effectively hard attention): upper end of the attention sweep.
Depth-3 variant (BETA=40, gate 100) with head logit scale 1 instead of 10: output margin check in the 3-block model.
Depth-3 variant (BETA=40, logit scale 10) with big-M gating constant 1000: loose-bound check that the gate is exact for any large M.
